course_name_original: Modelos Matemáticos y Estadísticos en Ingeniería
course_name_en: Mathematical and Statistical Models in Engineering
prerequisites: It is advisable to have acquired the competences of the basic training module of the degree.
Interest in the application of mathematical and statistical techniques for solving engineering problems.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Communicate the process and solution, interpreting and visualizing the results if possible.
Recognize and model problems in industry that can be solved or explained using mathematical or statistical models.
Know and apply numerical methods for solving initial value problems and boundary value problems.
Know and apply different models for solving partial differential equations.
Solve problems using mathematical and statistical models with a computer.

syllabus_topics: Block 1: Function approximation. 1.1 Least squares approximation. 1.2 Approximation by trigonometric polynomials. 1.3 Fast Fourier Transform, FFT.
Block 2: Numerical methods for solving differential equations. 2.1 Euler's method. 2.2 Runge-Kutta methods. 2.3 Systems of equations.

Block 3: Numerical methods for solving partial differential equations. 3.1 Finite difference method for elliptic equations. Laplace's equation. 3.2 Finite difference method for parabolic equations. Explicit methods and implicit methods.

Block 4: Basic Concepts of Statistical Inference. 4.1 Objectives of Statistical Inference. 4.2 Statistics and Estimators. 4.3 Properties of estimators. Distributions of the most common estimators. 4.4 Confidence intervals.
Block 5: Regression models. 5.1 Simple linear regression. 5.2 Multiple linear regression.
Block 6: Multivariate Analysis Techniques. 6.1 Factor Analysis. 6.2 Cluster Analysis. 6.3 Discriminant Analysis.

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring and control activities (written tests with practical exercises and student work follow-up)
Final test (theoretical and practical knowledge exercises)
